source.title: Self-Recognition Finetuning can Reverse and Prevent Emergent Misalignment

record.tranche_reason: Tests narrow-task fine-tuning and a benign fine-tuning intervention, but uses binary TruthfulQA rather than the original free-form misalignment evaluation.
record.gate_note: The post reports results mainly in figures whose plotted values are not included in the supplied text. The text does describe the direction of several effects. No exact scores are recoverable. The authors also note that binary TruthfulQA does not check answer coherence. Rows use “figure only” where no value is supplied.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes three chat models on narrow EM datasets (aesthetic preferences, risky financial, bad medical advice) and reports misalignment on binary TruthfulQA. This bears on V2. It also applies benign fine-tunes before or after EM, both self-recognition and a longer-summary control, which bears on V6's benign re-training part. The measure differs from the original free-form evaluation, coherence is not checked, and values appear only in figures.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that EM is entangled with model identity: EM suppresses self-recognition, identity system prompts modulate EM, and identity confusion worsens it. They report that self-recognition fine-tuning prevents and reverses EM. They attribute its effect to its metacognitive nature, because a same-format non-metacognitive SFT had negligible effect. They acknowledge that binary TruthfulQA does not check coherence and promise further evaluations.
record.recipe_differences: Uses narrow EM fine-tuning datasets and Axolotl, but evaluates with binary TruthfulQA rather than free-form answers; adds SGTR, identity-confusion, system-prompt, and non-metacognitive-SFT interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: EM results vary by dataset. Removing Qwen’s default system prompt during EM training reduces the measured effect; matching prompts improve reversal but weaken mitigation. The authors report five random seeds, but not seed-level outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: EM fine-tuning drops pairwise self-recognition to about 50% in all three models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow EM fine-tuning impairs a model's recognition of its own outputs.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing Qwen's default identity system prompt from EM training data reduces TruthfulQA misalignment; the size of the reduction varies by dataset.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For Qwen models, the system prompt present during EM fine-tuning modulates EM strength.

fits_no_version.finding: Identity-confusion training (random self-recognition labels) combined with EM increases misalignment; GPT-4.1 matching variants were blocked after safety evals.
ICTR alone gave small misalignment in early GPT-4.1 runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A narrow fine-tune on identity confusion alone may induce some misalignment.

record.problems: Misalignment is measured with binary TruthfulQA, which the authors acknowledge does not check coherence. The post says further evaluations are intended. Most reported values are only in figures and are absent from the supplied text. GPT-4.1 could not be fine-tuned on the financial and medical datasets through the API. The longer-summary control is not a clean non-metacognitive control for GPT-4.1 because its summaries were consistently longer. Five seeds are reported, but no per-seed results are given here.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. r19 is retained as an explicitly unavailable model mismatch noted in the text only to clarify that Figure 4 covers Qwen models; it has no outcome and should not be used as evidence.

untested.parts: Insecure code appears only as a system-prompt ablation on Qwen-Coder, without matched controls or free-form evaluation.
Reward hacks and number sequences are not tested. Free-form misaligned answers appear only in an unreported comment figure.
No linear direction or persona-feature analysis.
Inoculation framing during EM training is not tested.
No per-seed outcomes, size sweep, coherence filtering, or training-time analysis.

record.verdict_notes: This is a blog post, and all quantitative results are figure-only. Commenters question whether the effects are statistically significant, note that the aesthetic dataset gives weak EM, and say TruthfulQA confounds capability with propensity. The non-metacognitive control was invalid for GPT-4.1, so the V6 challenge covers Qwen and Seed only. A commenter notes this negligible-control result conflicts with prior reports that EM is easily trained out with benign samples.

versions.untested_parts: The insecure-code result is not reported as a free-form-answer measure, and the study does not compare it with secure-code or class-requested insecure-code controls.

Tests unpopular aesthetic preferences, risky financial advice, and bad medical advice, but not reward hacks or number sequences; GPT-4.1 results are limited to the aesthetic-preferences dataset. Uses TruthfulQA rather than misaligned free-form answers.
Does not test a shared linear direction or persona feature mediating EM across fine-tunes.
Tests self-recognition fine-tuning before or after EM, but not inoculation framing that explicitly requests bad behavior. The result is measured with binary TruthfulQA.
Reports results for three models and says experiments used five random seeds, but does not provide per-seed outcomes, a size sweep, coherence-filtered results, or a training-step sweep.
